reasoning_traces.think:
Elo operates as an online gradient descent algorithm minimizing binary cross-entropy loss under a logistic link function. Its regret bound (1/T)Regret_T ≤ C√(N/T) implies that in sparse settings—where T/N is small—simple models like Elo outperform complex ones such as pairwise or Glicko due to lower variance and reduced overfitting. The model misspecification term dominates in nonstationary or non-BT environments, but the regret component remains bounded, ensuring long-term consistency. The sparsity rule t/N < 1000 favors Elo because it minimizes cumulative loss through its convex structure and bounded regret. In contrast, Elo2k’s non-convexity introduces instability in high-dimensional parameter spaces, making it less reliable when data is insufficient. Thus, the paper establishes a principled framework for model selection based on data density rather than arbitrary complexity.
